step4MergedIncrements.acceptanceEvidenceCaveat: Acceptance evidence differs per pull request and must not be generalized. Pull requests 44, 46, 47, 49, 50, 51, 52, and 53: the conversation threads were inspected on 2026-09-02 and no owner-acceptance artifact was found, so the merge commit is the only acceptance-relevant artifact; the owner comments on 47, 49, 50, and 51 are supersession and findings-response notes, not acceptance. Pull request 48: carries an owner comment accepting the ADR-029 architecture decision only, which explicitly does not accept every pull request 47/48 implementation detail and does not establish responsive, RTL, reduced-motion, accessibility, or visual-regression completion for sequence items L to O. Pull requests 55, 56, 57, 58, and 59: carry owner-acceptance comments at their exact reviewed candidate heads. Pull request 57 additionally records independent read-only verification G3 APPROVE and a passing Frontend CI run at its accepted head; neither 57 nor 58 authorizes any follow-on task, and 58 explicitly does not establish production visual acceptance, live CMS validation, verify:alignment, or L to O QA. Pull request 59 additionally records a passing Frontend CI run at its accepted head and, per the owner comment, an independent review returning APPROVE; its acceptance covers G to J branch variant validation only. A merge is not by itself evidence of owner acceptance. This list is exact; pull request 45 is an unrelated open draft and is not part of it.
step4MergedIncrements.acceptanceEvidenceMethod: recordedReviews counts formal GitHub Review objects only. A count of 0 states that no Review object was submitted; it does not establish absence of owner-acceptance evidence, because pull request conversation comments are durable acceptance evidence, as pull requests 48, 55, and 56 demonstrate. Review-object count and acceptance evidence are separate facts and must be evaluated separately for each pull request.
